intro.after: can cut latency and spend without changing your model.
intro.before: Every repeated call to an LLM costs money and time, so

bullets.text: Hashes prompt + model + settings into a key and looks it up in Redis
A hit returns in about a millisecond and spends zero tokens
Only replays what the model already said for that exact input
One changed character is a miss, so hit rates are low for free-form chat

items.diagram: Prompt 'What is 2+2?' hashes to key 'a1b2' storing response '4'. Same prompt again hashes to 'a1b2' and instantly returns '4'.
items.title: Exact-Match Caching

bullets.text: Reuses the nearest cached answer if similarity clears a threshold (0.85)
Catches rewordings like “Capital of France?” vs “What’s France’s capital?”
A higher threshold means fewer hits but fewer mistakes; tune it on real logs
False hits: “refund order 123” and “refund order 456” look alike but differ

items.diagram: Embed 'Capital of France?' as a vector. New query 'What's France's capital?' lands close (similarity above threshold) so cached 'Paris' is returned.
items.title: Semantic Caching

bullets.text: Keeps the attention state of a shared prompt start and skips recomputing it
Here 1,022 prompt tokens drop to 522 computed: a faster first token
vLLM (automatic prefix caching) and SGLang (RadixAttention) do it for you
An early change (a timestamp, a user name) breaks the cache after it

items.diagram: A 500-token system prompt is shared by 'Q1' and 'Q2'. The engine caches compute for the shared 500 tokens and only processes each differing suffix.
items.title: Prefix Caching

bullets.text: Stores each token’s key and value vectors, so each step computes only the new token
Without it, every step recomputes K and V for all earlier tokens (quadratic work)
vLLM’s PagedAttention stores it in blocks, cutting wasted memory to under 4%
Grows with length: Llama-2-7B needs ~0.5 MB per token, ~2 GB for a 4K context

items.diagram: Decoding token 1 stores K,V per layer. Generating token 2 reuses the stored K,V for token 0-1 and only computes K,V for the new token.
items.title: KV-Cache Reuse

bullets.text: Marks a big block (docs, tools, system prompt) as cacheable across calls
Cache reads are billed at a discount (10% of input price on most Claude models)
OpenAI does it automatically for prompts of 1,024+ tokens
Rules vary by vendor: minimum size, TTL (5 min on Claude), write fees

items.diagram: Upload a 50-page PDF once with a cache flag. The next 10 calls reference the cache id and skip re-reading the PDF's tokens.
items.title: Provider Context Cache

bullets.text: Dedupes identical rows first: 10,000 tickets become 3,000 calls (70% fewer)
Batch APIs add a 50% discount on top, with results within 24 hours
Stores results by input hash, so the next run only pays for new or changed rows
Offline only: batches can take hours, so they can’t serve a live user

items.diagram: 10,000 support tickets dedupe to 3,000 unique texts, the LLM runs once per unique text, and results map back to all 10,000 rows.
items.title: Batch Response Caching

overview.side: Batch caching happens outside the live request path, deduping upfront.

data.overview_title: Where each cache strategy plugs in

principles.sub: Add a hash-keyed cache before anything else; it's free latency savings.
Tune the similarity threshold and test for false-positive wrong answers.
Use vLLM or provider caching instead of reinventing attention reuse.

quote.big: Cache the compute, not just the text.
quote.small: Six layers, one goal: skip redundant LLM calls.
